sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Live bootleg titles: release and release group titles are checked against MusicBrainz's live bootleg convention "YYYY-MM-DD[, early show]: Venue, City, State, Country" (https://musicbrainz.org/doc/Style/Specific_types_of_releases/Live_bootlegs). On the same columns that carry the "Title info" sections (every Title column plus "Unique-Values Dropdown: Title Info On These Columns Too"), the 📊 dropdown gets new "Live title info" sections: Validity (valid / impossible date, with the release status added on a status sub-table such as a release group's "Bootleg release"), Near miss (titles that start with a date but are not in the live form, e.g. "05.02.1975: …" or a missing ": "), Date completeness (complete / incomplete, and one entry per date shape: YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM, YYYY, MM-DD, with ?? for an unknown part), Additional date info ("early show", …), and three Separator sections, one each for dates written only with "‐" (U+2010), only with a plain "-", or with both, each repeating the valid / impossible / incomplete / additional-info counts. Every entry filters the table. Behind the new setting "Unique-Values Dropdown: Live Title Info" (on by default).

Live bootleg titles: cells are tinted light red with a ❌ when the date is impossible (month 13, day 42, 29 February in a non-leap year) or the title is a near miss, and light yellow with a ⚠️ when the date uses a plain "-" anywhere between its parts. Red wins over yellow. The tooltip says what is wrong. Each tint has its own setting: "Live Titles: Flag Invalid Dates And Near Misses" and "Live Titles: Flag ASCII Date Separators" (both on by default). The tint is applied once per load, so filtering and sorting cost nothing extra.
